implementation: Readable RAM-backed finite-decimal Richardson differentiation with ordered paired copies and live-mode X publication.
limits: The tested expression adapter preserves syntax/cursor, callback finishing, evaluator-error publication, cancellation and saved-X restoration. Uncovered mode-changing callbacks and arbitrary CPU-frame aliases remain unproven.
The core preserves paired transfers but performs scalar ten-byte arithmetic; this does not implement ordinary complex differentiation.
Full persistent RAM and native B exhaustion are not established by the prepared core corpus.

verification.scope: Prepared point/tolerance and core effects on production sources; whole expression binding has its separate proof below.

expression_verification.check_units: Includes individual persistent RAM-byte comparisons; this is not instruction coverage.
expression_verification.limits: Original observed CPU frame excluded; bounded corpus, not general complex differentiation.
